parsed.explanation: The quote is verbatim, but the objection attacks a strawman: the text never claims (4) is literally symmetric in x,y; it says 'up to the roles of c,e and the sign of the linear term', which is exactly the relabelling the objector concedes works. The inference is valid: (4) holds for all ordered pairs (x,y)>0, so re-instantiating it with x from the e-orbit and y from the c-orbit re-runs the identical computation with c↔e, x₀↔y₀; in Case 1 this yields const + 4pe(e−c)k → −∞ when c>e. Equivalently, the hypotheses ('two positive values with chosen base points') are symmetric, so 'WLOG c<e' is a complete standard justification. The objector supplies no counterexample and no invalid inference, and admits the relabelling works; the only complaint is terseness, which is not an error. Even if sustained, the step is an inessential one-line relabelling.
